subject: How to select specific hours in an analysis ?

messages.author: d6d7243b8d5b18cd
messages.subject: How to select specific hours in an analysis ?
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I have one week of accelerometer data for my participants, strictly starting on Tuesday (16 pm) and finishing on Sunday (23:59 pm) for each participant.

I would like to compute physical activity scores representing mean physical activity performed from Tuesday to Friday only in the evening, precisely between 17 pm and sleep (an arbitrary threshold such as 23:59 pm could also be suitable), 

How can I do that ? Vincent tell me that it is in the g.part5 but even with this information I can't solve this problem, 

Thanks in advance for your help, as well as the development and maintenance of this package, 

Cheers !

Guillaume

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] How to select specific hours in an analysis ?
parts:
Hi Guillaume, 
I overlooked your desired to calculate this between 5pm and sleep. This is not faciltiated directly in GGIR, but you can use the milestone data stored in the 'meta' subfolder of the output to compute it yourself.
This data includes epoch by epoch values of acceleration and timestamp, which is what you need to derive those variables.
Cheers
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: How to select specific hours in an analysis ?
parts:
Thanks Vincent, 

I have one more question please, 

When you specify the argument "ilevels", for example c(50, 100) ; we have the output "(50,100)_mg_0-24h_ENMO" which give us the time spent between these thresholds. However this output it's not comparable for example with the mvpa point "MVPA_E5S_B10M80%_T100_ENMO" ; so how can I obtained a similar score (e.g., E5S_B10M80%) but for ENMO comprise between 50 and 100 ? I can do that with gpart2 or I need gpart5 ? 

Thanks a lot,

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: How to select specific hours in an analysis ?
parts:
Hi Guillaume,
Part 2 only offers a basic version of MVPA bouts, which is the one use for the da Silva IJE paper on the Pelotas Cohorts. If you want to look at bouts of 50 - 100 ENMO mg which could correspond to light activity then you will need part 5. Thanks, Vincent
If you have more questions, please post them on github: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues
